Can you explain why? What is the fix to avoid it always doing nothing?
I guess that works. Although I'd leave out the must since it's not a requirement on anyone, it's just a definition. Similarly to how they have a url, instead of must have a url.
Because we need to do the structured clone that the URL parser does at a specific point in time. I agree that something is wrong here though.
OK. We need to check this against implementations then, if you think that's how they work. Adam was pretty explicit that the only reactive changes were for styling.
Implementations are notably wrong for blob URLs.
Well, we need to find in what ways they're willing to change. Speaking from my minor implementation experience in jsdom, this is an extremely expensive requirement as specced.
If we don't do this blob URLs will effectively be a major memory leak forever. Though note that since it only affects blob URLs, implementations can take numerous shortcuts.

For example, it seems fine to have blob URL structured cloning happen when you do a getter. It's maybe a bit unpredictable, but it's deterministic and can be interoperably implemented, while not tanking performance of common DOM manipulations and parsing.

Again, I'm not as familiar with this blob URL situation as you are. Could you explain how it causes them to be a major memory leak forever?

This does seem like something that we really want implementer consensus on how to solve, as it involves definite tradeoffs, which implementers have not been interested in implementing so far. Maybe open a separate issue if you think it must be included in this PR?
It's very much non-deterministic. It could basically depend on whether the user clicked the link on time.
Yeah, I agree it probably warrants more discussion.
Why? That doesn't seem true to me at all, following the algorithms. Also, that's not non-deterministic, if you've specced that in reaction to clicking links this happens.
